title: Downhole-200C Ga2O3 vertical gain-cell tiers become refresh-free at room temperature
idea: Design the cell for a 200 C oil-well logging tool: a capacitor-less 2T gain cell whose write and read transistors are vertical beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV bandgap) pillars at 4F2, stacked 8-16 tiers over CMOS by low-temperature ALD. A cell qualified to hold charge 10 ms at 200 C holds it for many minutes at 85 C, so the same array ships to datacenters with refresh essentially gone.
why: Attacks the leakage tail and refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor wall (fact 1); recovers 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth, and 4F2 vertical stacking gives ~3-8x bits per mm2.

title: Well-less satellite tiers: oxide-isolated array layers remove STI for 4F2
idea: Satellites dodge single-event upsets by putting transistors on buried oxide with no bulk well; build every DRAM array tier on transferred thin silicon over oxide so there is no substrate junction, no well contact and no shallow-trench isolation between cells. Gate-all-around vertical channels abut at true 4F2 because isolation comes from the oxide below, and the bulk charge-collection volume behind soft errors and junction leakage disappears.
why: Layout density 6F2 to 4F2 (~33% more bits per tier), removes the junction/GIDL part of the retention tail (fact 3), and gives inherent soft-error immunity.

title: LN2-immersed memory pods with planar 0.5 fF capacitors, 100 tiers
idea: Design for a 77 K cryogenic computer: access-transistor leakage falls ~10^6x, so retention stops sizing the capacitor and, with 64-cell short bitlines, a flat 0.5 fF planar MIM capacitor suffices, making each tier a thin planar layer and 100-tier monolithic stacks practical. Ship the memory as liquid-nitrogen-immersed CXL pods beside the accelerator (nitrogen is abundant and cheap).
why: Removes the AR 60-75:1 capacitor (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3) and clears the 26+ tier break-even for 3D (fact 2) with planar tiers; claim 5-10x bits per mm2, with cooling overhead paid only on low-dissipation memory pods.

title: Qubit-control superconducting wordlines shrink sub-wordline driver strips
idea: Control memory for 4 K quantum computers can use NbTiN wordlines with no resistive RC, so one sub-wordline driver can span 8x more cells; at 77 K the same floorplan uses copper or YBCO-strapped wordlines whose resistivity drops 5-7x. Re-floorplan the mats with 4-8x longer wordline segments so the driver strips that tile the array shrink proportionally.
why: Periphery takes ~49% of the die (fact 7): cutting sub-wordline driver strips 4x frees ~8-12% of die area and gives a cold-memory floorplan that generalizes.

title: Vertical CCD charge-shift strings as append-only KV-cache memory
idea: An AI KV-cache is written once in order and read back as a stream, so build a 3D-NAND-like vertical string but run it as a charge-coupled device: 128 stacked gate tiers around one channel pass charge packets along the string by 3-phase clocking to a single sense node at the top. There is no per-cell access transistor, capacitor or contact; a bit is just one gate crossing.
why: Density ~30-50x bits per mm2 vs planar 6F2, no capacitor (fact 1), periphery amortized over 128 bits per string (fact 7), and no per-bit bitline swing (fact 8); latency is sequential, which suits KV traffic.

title: Retention-tiered monolithic stack with minutes-retention tiers for KV data
idea: Serve the AI KV-cache user whose data lives seconds to minutes: in one monolithic 3D stack the lower tiers use a thicker tunnel barrier around a charge-storage gate (minutes retention, slower write) while the top tiers keep fast capacitor cells, and the controller places each KV block by expected lifetime. The tier recipes differ in a single dielectric thickness, so it remains one process flow.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3) vanishes for the long-lived bulk of KV data and capacitor-free tiers are denser (fact 1); ~2-4x capacity per die at similar cost.

title: Two-mask-per-tier self-aligned crosspoint gain cell for $1 IoT
idea: A $1 IoT chip cannot afford 30 masks, so define every memory tier with exactly two orthogonal line masks, as in crosspoint memory: line set A forms the write wordline plus storage gate, line set B forms the bitline plus vertical channel, and a 2T gain cell self-aligns at every crossing. All tiers reuse the same two masks.
why: Mask count and capital (fact 4): 2 masks per tier instead of 5-7 EUV layers, 4F2 per crossing, ~2-3x lower cost per bit at mature nodes, and memory buildable in the BEOL over a cheap MCU.

title: Hot-spare tiers from 30-year industrial controllers raise stack yield
idea: An industrial controller must run 30 years unserviced, so each 3D array carries two spare tiers and a per-mat tier-remap table in the bonded logic layer; a failing tier is retired in the field and its data copied to a spare. In the fab the same mechanism lets a 64-tier stack ship with any two bad tiers.
why: Tier-count yield blocks 3D DRAM (fact 2): 0.99^64 = 53% compound tier yield rises to ~97% with two spares, ~1.5x lower cost per bit.

title: Artillery-fuze lesson: mold-retained honeycomb braces AR-120 capacitors
idea: Artillery-fuze electronics survive 20,000 g by having no unsupported tall structure; likewise keep the oxide mold in place as a hexagonal honeycomb that braces every storage node, so tall electrodes cannot lean, bend or stick during wet cleans. Electrodes line each honeycomb cup, and the extra height (AR 120 instead of ~65) more than repays the lost outer surface.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): reaches the needed AR ~115 without pattern collapse, ~1.4x Cs or ~20% tighter pitch.

title: Pixel-detector bonding: every 16 bitlines get their own sense-amp bond
idea: Particle-physics pixel detectors bond each sensor pixel to its own readout channel; hybrid-bond the DRAM array wafer at ~0.4 um pitch so every group of 16 bitlines, muxed by an in-array selector, lands on its own sense amplifier on a separately made logic wafer. The array wafer then holds no sense amps, decoders or I/O at all.
why: Periphery ~49% of the die (fact 7) moves to a cheap logic wafer: ~2x array-wafer area per bit, and logic-process sense amps run faster at lower voltage (fact 10).

title: Stacked-sensor sandwich: wordline drivers bonded above, sense amps below
idea: Three-layer stacked camera sensors showed a thinned die can be bonded on both faces; thin the DRAM array wafer to ~3 um, hybrid-bond a wordline-driver wafer to its top face and a sense-amp wafer to its bottom face, so wordlines exit upward and bitlines exit downward. The two peripheries never compete for one routing plane, the array die is ~100% cells, and both periphery wafers use logic processes.
why: Periphery and routing congestion (fact 7): array efficiency ~51% to ~95%, ~1.6x lower bit cost, and low-voltage logic periphery cuts energy (fact 10).

title: Pacemaker nanowatt array: 8-tier vertical bitlines with local gain
idea: A pacemaker budget means tiny bitline swings; give each vertical bitline only 8 tiers of cells and a one-transistor gain stage at its base, so local bitline capacitance is ~0.1 fF and a 1 fF capacitor still develops ~450 mV. The gain stage alone drives the long global bitline.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): Cs can drop ~5x to ~1 fF, a shallow capacitor that fits lateral 3D tiers (fact 2); bitline energy down ~10x (fact 10).

title: LIGO-style differential cell: true and complement capacitors stacked vertically
idea: Ultra-low-noise instruments sense differentially; store each bit as true and complement charge on two capacitors stacked one above the other in the same 4F2 footprint, a bottom-tier and a top-tier transistor sharing one vertical pillar, read by a reference-free differential amplifier. Signal doubles and reference and offset noise cancel, so each capacitor can be half the size.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): each capacitor ~2.5 fF at about half the aspect ratio (~35:1), easing the hardest etch while footprint density holds; immune to reference drift.

title: HFT dual-port cell: capacitor sandwiched between two vertical transistors
idea: High-frequency traders cannot tolerate refresh stalls; build a vertical cell whose capacitor sits between a bottom access transistor on bitline A, owned by a refresh/scrub engine, and a top access transistor on bitline B, owned by the host. Stacking makes the second port free in footprint, so refresh, row-hammer mitigation and ECC scrub run on port A while port B serves traffic.
why: Refresh bandwidth loss of 10-20% (fact 3) and row-hammer mitigation stalls (fact 9) become invisible; deterministic latency and ~10-20% more usable bandwidth per die.

title: Whole DRAM wafer bonded onto a wafer-scale accelerator
idea: Wafer-scale computers already route around defects; hybrid-bond an undiced 300 mm DRAM wafer face-to-face onto a wafer-scale accelerator with bonds at every compute tile and map out bad mats in the routing fabric. Each tile reads the DRAM directly above it over millimeter-scale wires.
why: Data movement (fact 5): 3-4 pJ/bit HBM to ~0.1-0.2 pJ/bit; HBM TSV tax (fact 6), dicing and packaging removed; ~1 TB at multi-TB/s per wafer.

title: Row-hammer adversary design: tier-interleaved rows with grounded shield planes
idea: Design for a malicious user who hammers rows: map logically adjacent rows onto different tiers of a 3D array and insert grounded metal shield planes between tiers, so no aggressor shares a tier or electrostatic coupling path with its logical neighbors. The memory controller's address hash enforces the tier interleave.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): coupling-driven flips pushed from ~1k toward >100k activations, removing TRR/RFM overhead (~5-10% bandwidth) and the attack surface.

title: Reactor-robot vacuum-gap access transistors for near-zero off-current
idea: Robots inside reactors use vacuum electronics because vacuum has no lattice to damage; make each access device a vertical nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor, a ~10 nm emitter tip facing a collector inside a ring gate, sealed in its 4F2 pillar when the tier is capped. With no conducting medium, off-state current is only zero-bias field emission, essentially nothing.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3) eliminated, radiation-immune, and tiny capacitors become viable (fact 1); claim retention of hours.

title: Thermal-cycling satellite stack with doped-silicon vias, no copper or tungsten
idea: Satellites cycle -150 to +120 C and copper vias crack silicon through CTE mismatch; build through-tier and through-die vias from degenerately doped epitaxial or poly silicon and fusion-bond Si to Si, so the whole stack is one CTE-matched material. Vias are fat but short because tiers are thinned to a few um.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) from vias and Cu-pumping keep-out zones, shrinking the TSV area tax (fact 6) ~2x and raising stack reliability.

title: Brain-implant heat rule: DRAM-logic tile mosaic stitched by bonded bridges
idea: A brain implant may not warm tissue 1 C, so heat must never pool under memory; instead of stacking DRAM on hot logic, tile 1 mm DRAM and logic chiplets in a checkerboard mosaic and stitch adjacent edges with a hybrid-bonded bridge die carrying thousands of sub-100 um links. Every logic tile touches four DRAM tiles while no DRAM sits above a hotspot.
why: DRAM runs ~20-30 C cooler than HBM-on-logic, cutting refresh 4-8x (fact 3), with ~0.3 pJ/bit data movement (fact 5).

title: Hyperscaler exabyte buyer: undiced DRAM wafers as rack memory slabs
idea: For the buyer who orders memory by the petabyte, skip dicing, per-die test and packaging: add a redistribution layer to a whole 300 mm DRAM wafer, route it to edge connectors, map bad mats in an on-wafer controller strip, and mount the bare wafer on a liquid cold plate in a CXL memory sled. A wafer of 16 Gb dies is ~1.5 TB in one field-replaceable unit.
why: Cost per bit: packaging, test and module costs (~15-25%) removed, and mat-level map-out replaces discarding whole dies (~5-10% more good bits).

title: Cheapest-bit market: convert idle 3D NAND lines to vertical-string DRAM
idea: Design for the buyer of the cheapest possible bits (the $50 laptop market): 3D NAND fabs already run 200+ tier staircase, channel-hole and replacement-gate tools on DUV only, so retool idle NAND lines to build vertical-string DRAM at relaxed F~40 nm with 64 tiers. License a cell that keeps the NAND tool set and swaps only the channel and storage modules.
why: Capital intensity and EUV dependence (fact 4): reuses $10B+ of installed tools, no EUV, and capacity in ~1-2 years instead of 3-5.

title: Automotive tier-RAID: erasure code striped across stacked array tiers
idea: Automotive ASIL-D allows no silent bit loss at 150 C; stripe each 64-byte line across 9 tiers of a 3D array (8 data + 1 parity) read in parallel, so any single tier with weak or hammered cells is rebuilt on the fly. Refresh can then be set by the typical tier rather than the worst cell anywhere in the stack.
why: The leakage tail sets refresh (fact 3): ~4x longer refresh interval because single-tier tail failures are corrected; tier yield (fact 2) improves at ~12% parity overhead.

title: Hearing-aid origami: fold one thinned DRAM strip into eight-high stack
idea: Hearing aids fit electronics by folding flex circuits; thin a strip of 8 DRAM die segments to ~10 um so the silicon flexes, pattern polymer-copper hinge interconnects between segments, and fold it accordion-style into a stack bonded with thin adhesive. The fold edges carry hundreds of wires per mm and replace TSVs for capacity-oriented stacks.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): TSV keep-out area and TSV yield loss (20-30%) removed, and stacking becomes a back-end assembly step.

title: Satellite-lot nanoimprint tiers: periodic arrays without excimer or EUV
idea: Space programs build memory in lots too small to amortize EUV, and EUV and ArF sources consume neon, helium, krypton or argon; a DRAM array layer is a perfectly periodic line or hole lattice, so print it by jet-and-flash nanoimprint cured with UV LEDs and write only the small non-periodic periphery with a multi-beam electron writer. Every tier reuses the same template, and transfer etches run on HBr/O2 chemistry with no argon dilution.
why: Removes 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) and the neon/helium supply risk; template ~10x cheaper than an EUV mask set and tool capex ~$30M vs $200M+.

title: $1-IoT block-copolymer pillar arrays guided by UV-LED exposure
idea: A $1 IoT memory needs dense pillars at near-zero patterning cost; spin a cylinder-forming block copolymer that self-assembles into a hexagonal ~22 nm pitch lattice of vertical-channel transistor sites, registered by coarse 200 nm guide posts printed with a 365 nm UV-LED stepper instead of a mercury-xenon lamp or excimer laser. Hexagonal packing gives slightly better than 4F2 density.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4) without EUV or rare-gas light sources; 4F2-class pillar arrays at <10% of EUV patterning cost.

title: Solar-cell economics: metal-assisted wet etching drills AR-200 capacitor holes
idea: Solar wafer makers texture silicon for cents with metal-assisted chemical etching; for DRAM, imprint a silver or platinum catalyst mesh and etch in HF/H2O2 at room temperature, which drills straight silicon holes at AR 200:1 with no plasma, no argon and no helium-cooled chuck. Line the holes with ALD electrode and high-k to form deep trench capacitors in each array tier.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 200 vs 60-75 gives ~2.5x Cs or a 2.5x smaller footprint, and the most expensive plasma etch and its rare gases are removed.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor heritage: self-ordered anodic alumina capacitor mold
idea: Thirty-year industrial power supplies rely on anodized aluminum's self-ordered pores; e-beam-evaporate aluminum (no argon sputter) over the array, pre-indent it by imprint to lock the pore sites to the ~40 nm cell pitch, and anodize it so straight nanopores at AR 300+ form in an electrolyte bath. ALD TiN/high-k/TiN into the pores to make one capacitor per landing pad.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 300 gives ~4x Cs or lets a lower-k dielectric work, using only wet anodization with no plasma etch or rare gas.

title: 300-layer NAND edge case: area-selective ALD molybdenum wordlines
idea: The tallest 3D NAND stacks already fill wordlines by CVD; take this further for 3D DRAM tiers with area-selective ALD molybdenum (MoCl5/H2 with nitrogen purge) that nucleates only on exposed seed edges in recessed lateral cavities while a self-assembled inhibitor blocks the oxide. No argon-sputtered liner, no tungsten and no wordline-isolation patterning step.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and argon PVD; void-free low-resistance lateral wordlines allow thinner tiers and more of them (fact 2).

title: Space cold-welding: atomic-hydrogen activated room-temperature Cu-Cu bonding
idea: In orbit, clean metals cold-weld on contact; reproduce this by reducing copper and SiCN bond surfaces with atomic hydrogen from a hot-filament H2 cracker in vacuum, instead of argon fast-atom beams or argon plasma, then pressing die to wafer at room temperature. No anneal is needed, so bonded DRAM tiers never see the 350-400 C that degrades retention.
why: Room-temperature bonding protects the leakage tail (fact 3), allows sub-0.5 um pitch with no copper expansion, and supports more bonded tiers (facts 2 and 6) without argon.

title: Giant-display lesson: blue diode lasers crystallize silicon for stacked tiers
idea: Gen-10 display fabs crystallize silicon over square meters with XeCl excimer lasers that consume xenon and neon; replace them with line-scanned 450 nm GaN diode-laser arrays to melt-crystallize thin amorphous silicon (PECVD in SiH4/H2) on top of each finished DRAM tier. The heat stays in ~100 nm, so lower tiers stay below 400 C while the new tier gets large-grain channels for its access transistors.
why: Monolithic tier stacking (fact 2) without a bond per tier and without xenon or neon; ~200 cm2/Vs channels for 3D cells.

title: KV-cache on display glass: mist-CVD oxide memory tiles from LCD fabs
idea: KV-cache buyers care about cost per bit far more than bits per mm2; build 3-tier oxide-channel 2T gain-cell arrays at relaxed 80 nm features on 2.2 x 2.5 m display glass in idle LCD fabs, depositing channels by atmospheric mist-CVD or nitrogen-purged ALD instead of argon-sputtered IGZO. Slice the panels into memory tiles hybrid-bonded to a logic bridge.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): display-fab area costs ~100x less per cm2 than DRAM wafer area, so even ~30x lower density gives several-fold cheaper bits for KV tiers, with no argon.

title: Grating-maker method: solid-state deep-UV interference lithography for arrays
idea: Makers of astronomical diffraction gratings print meter-scale periodic lines by interfering laser beams, with no mask; use a frequency-quintupled Nd:YAG (213 nm) or solid-state 193 nm laser, built on nonlinear crystals with no argon-fluoride or neon gas, in two-beam and four-beam interference to print the array's line and hole lattices at ~40 nm pitch. Spacer pitch-splitting then reaches ~20 nm.
why: EUV/ArF dependence and their He/Ne/Kr/Ar gases removed (fact 4); interference tool ~$5-10M vs $200M, ~5x lower array patterning cost per layer.

title: Reactor neutron-transmutation-doped donor wafers for transferred array tiers
idea: Power-device makers dope silicon in a nuclear reactor, turning Si-30 into phosphorus with near-perfect uniformity; NTD-dope the donor wafers whose thin layers are transferred to form junctionless n-type channel tiers, so channel doping is fixed before transfer. Array implants and their xenon or argon plasma flood guns are skipped.
why: Removes array doping implants and rare-gas flood-gun use, and eliminates CZ striations and implant dose drift; ~10-20% tighter Vt spread trims the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Rocket regenerative cooling: microchannels between bonded tiers allow 32-high
idea: Rocket nozzles survive by pumping coolant through channels in their own walls; wet-etch (TMAH, no plasma) 20 um microchannels into the backside of every fourth thinned DRAM die and bond with nitrogen-plasma-activated oxide instead of argon activation, so dielectric coolant flows through the stack and pulls heat from inside. Stacks grow to 24-32 high while staying below 85 C.
why: Layer count is thermally limited: cooler DRAM cuts refresh 2-4x (fact 3) and doubles capacity per stack, with argon-free bond activation.

title: Sanctioned-fab rule: film-thickness-defined cell replaces litho-defined pitch
idea: Design for a country cut off from EUV, ArF and neon: rotate the cell so every critical dimension is a deposited film thickness (channel length is an epitaxial layer, gate length a wordline film, cell pitch the tier pitch), and the only lithography is a 0.5 um UV-LED step that cuts slits and staircases. The cell is a lateral transistor plus lateral capacitor in each tier, like a rotated 3D NAND page.
why: Removes litho-bound scaling and EUV capital (fact 4): density comes from 64-100 tiers at 0.5 um lithography, roughly halving the 55% depreciation share.

title: Mars-ISRU gas whitelist as a rare-gas-free DRAM process kit
idea: A Mars fab could only use gases made from CO2, water and nitrogen; define a binding whitelist (N2, H2, O2, CO2, H2O, NH3, NF3, HF, HBr, Cl2, SiH4) and requalify every 3D-array step against it, publishing the recipes as an open process design kit. Make whitelist compliance a condition of federal fab grants so U.S. DRAM lines cannot be stopped by a helium, neon or xenon shock.
why: Helium (Qatar ~30% offline), neon and xenon chokepoints removed and U.S. manufacturability raised; a step change in supply resilience rather than cost.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling for cryogenic high-aspect-ratio etch, helium-free
idea: Etch tools cool wafers with helium between wafer and chuck; hydrogen conducts heat slightly better than helium, so run cryogenic (-110 C) SF6/O2 etch of capacitor holes and tier stacks with low-pressure H2 backside gas, using liquid-hydrogen rocket practice for sensors and inerted lines. Cryo etch passivates sidewalls with SiOxFy and needs no argon, giving vertical profiles at high AR.
why: Removes helium from every etch chamber; AR 100+ cryo etch for capacitors (fact 1) and tier stacks (fact 2) with better chuck uniformity.

title: Spin-qubit plasma-free fab: vapor-HCl carved lateral cells in Si/SiGe
idea: Silicon spin-qubit fabs avoid plasma damage; grow 3D DRAM tiers as an epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice in H2 carrier, open vertical slits by metal-assisted wet etch, then remove the SiGe selectively with gas-phase HCl to open lateral cavities where gate and capacitor stacks are deposited by ALD. No plasma ever touches the channel.
why: Lateral 3D DRAM transistor quality (fact 2): damage-free channels cut trap-assisted leakage tail (fact 3) ~3-10x, with no argon.

title: PCB-shop vacuum-free metallization for TSVs and through-tier vias
idea: Circuit-board shops metallize millions of vias with no vacuum; replace argon-sputtered Ta/Cu seed in TSVs and through-array vias with an electroless Ni-B barrier and an electroless copper seed grafted on a silane monolayer, then fill by bottom-up superconformal plating. The whole via flow runs at atmospheric pressure on wet benches.
why: HBM TSV cost (fact 6) and argon PVD removed; wet tools ~5x cheaper, and conformal seeds allow 20:1+ TSVs, shrinking TSV diameter and keep-out ~2x.

title: Defense low-volume rule: one template for every tier, decoded vertically
idea: Defense users need many small memory variants and each imprint template is precious; make every tier identical, printed with one template, and select tiers not with a staircase but with a chain of tier-select transistors in each vertical bitline pillar, driven by a decoder in the bonded logic die. Products differ only in tier count.
why: Staircase area (~5-10% of die) and the KrF/ArF resist-trim steps that need krypton, argon and neon disappear; one template for all tiers (fact 4).

title: MLCC-style nanolaminate storage capacitor with interdigitated ALD electrodes
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitors get high capacitance cheaply from hundreds of interleaved electrodes; build each DRAM storage node as an ALD nanolaminate of 6-10 alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers (nitrogen purge, no sputtering) in a lateral cavity, contacting odd electrodes on one side and even electrodes on the other by selective wet recess. Capacitance scales with layer count instead of aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~3-5x Cs per footprint without AR 115 or k 70, sized for lateral 3D DRAM tiers (fact 2).

title: Undersea-fiber draw: thermally drawn preform sliced into vertical memory arrays
idea: Fiber makers draw a macroscopic preform 100,000x into kilometers of perfectly periodic structure; assemble a centimeter preform holding a lattice of silicon cores, glass gate insulator and metal-alloy gate lines, draw it in nitrogen to ~50 nm core pitch, then slice the rod into wafers whose silicon cores become vertical channels finished by ALD. No lithography or rare gas is used for the array.
why: Array lithography and EUV capital (fact 4) eliminated; speculative ~10x lower cost per bit if drawn cores recrystallize to device grade.

title: Accelerator ion tracks etched into ultra-deep capacitor holes
idea: Accelerator users make track-etch membranes where each swift heavy ion leaves a straight damage trail that etches into an AR >1000 pore; irradiate a thick oxide or polymer mold through a registered silicon stencil with gold or bismuth ions (not xenon or krypton beams) and etch the tracks into one ultra-deep hole per cell. Several tracks per stencil opening merge to beat Poisson placement statistics.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 200-500 gives 3-6x Cs with no plasma etch and no rare-gas ion species.

title: Deep-sea pressure: high-pressure deuterium anneal heals stacked-tier traps
idea: Deep-ocean hardware shows how pressure drives gas into solids; anneal finished 3D DRAM tier stacks in 20-50 atm deuterium/nitrogen at <=400 C so deuterium penetrates many tiers and passivates the channel and interface traps behind the leakage tail, staying within the stack's thermal budget. Deuterium bonds resist hot-carrier and activation-stress depassivation.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): tail traps cut ~2-5x, lengthening refresh; trap-assisted row hammer (fact 9) reduced; no argon or helium ambient.

title: Kerfless-solar epitaxial lift-off: crucible-free crystalline tiers from reusable parents
idea: Kerfless solar startups grow epitaxial silicon on porous-silicon release layers and peel it, reusing the parent wafer many times; grow 1 um device-grade epi in H2-carrier trichlorosilane on a porous parent, bond it onto the finished DRAM stack, cleave at the porous layer to form the next tier, and re-porosify the parent for ~50 reuses. This replaces smart-cut, whose co-implants often use helium.
why: Spruce Pine quartz-crucible dependence cut ~50x per tier, crystalline bonded tiers for 3D DRAM (fact 2), helium-free.

title: RFID fluidic self-assembly: shaped DRAM tiles settle into logic sockets
idea: Five-cent RFID tags place millions of chips by letting shaped dies settle into matching wells in a liquid flow; dice DRAM arrays into 0.5 mm trapezoidal tiles, flow them over a logic wafer with matching recesses and hydrophilic capillary pads, then hybrid-bond in nitrogen. Logic wafers get stacked memory at wafer throughput with no pick-and-place and no argon plasma activation.
why: Die-to-wafer bonding throughput and cost (fact 6) improve ~10-100x, known-good tiles raise stack yield vs wafer-to-wafer, and memory directly over logic cuts data movement (fact 5).
